decisions.question: How do customers without an MDM evidence EP-02, EP-03, EP-05 and EP-06, which today only people can satisfy (and F1 means the device artifact cannot be satisfied at all)?
options: A. Verity agent (Go plus osquery): system generated and continuous, serves anyone who installs it, each person installs and grants permissions, Verity builds agent, installers, signing, notarization, updates, ingestion and support, explicitly out of scope today, cannot enforce or wipe
B. MDM connectors only: system generated, continuous and enforced, serves only customers with an MDM, connect once, cannot see unenrolled devices

C. Reviewed device attestation: self reported with OS screenshots or command output and approved by a reviewer, serves everyone, each person every quarter, smallest build (a form, a review queue, reminders), cannot prove continuity between attestations

D. Google Endpoint Verification: system generated and continuous but not enforced, serves Google Workspace customers, turn on and staff add the extension, a few fields on the Phase 2 Workspace connector, cannot report screen lock timeout or wipe laptops
decisions.recommendation: Do not build an agent now. Use Google Endpoint Verification where the customer runs Google Workspace (free on almost every edition), Intune where the customer already pays for Microsoft 365 Business Premium or E3, and the structured, reviewed device attestation (C) everywhere else as the universal fallback, so every endpoint control can be completed without a connector. defects.finding: _ingest does 'unmatched += 1; continue', so a finding on an unregistered host disappears and the register looks cleaner than the estate.
defects.proposal: NEED verity_vulnerabilities: findings on hosts not in the asset register are kept as unmatched and raise asset register work (LM-01, proposed LM-13).

defects.finding: first_detected_at=now: the SLA starts when Verity first sees the finding, not when the scanner found it, so a first sync of an old backlog shows nothing overdue.

defects.finding: _SEVERITY_WORDS maps 0..4 and a few words; anything else becomes medium, so Rapid7 'severe' and Qualys level 5 would be stored as medium.

defects.finding: verify_instance closes only from pending_retest, by a person; a fix the scanner confirmed stays open until someone clicks.

defects.finding: SOC2:CC7.1 and ISO27001:A.8.8 are full on LM-11, which bundles discovery coverage with triage, remediation and acceptance (different owners, cadences and failure conclusions).

defects.finding: Repeated BC-07.C (register complete).
defects.proposal: Reword to tiering: each supplier with access has a current tier that sets the depth of its assessment.

defects.finding: Tested a population of merges only, though ISO27001:A.8.19 and A.8.32 rely on SD-01 for server software, infrastructure, configuration and database changes.
defects.proposal: Reword to cover the whole change population, with the proposed infrastructure-and-configuration-change-history artifact.

defects.finding: ISO27001:A.8.28 and A.8.29 rely on static analysis in the pipeline; no objective tested that it ran. SD-02.E applies only with Processing Integrity.
defects.proposal: Add SD-02.F; SD-02.E reads not applicable when Processing Integrity is out of scope.

defects.finding: Bundled the component list with licences (ISO27001:A.5.32) into the dependency triage standard.
defects.proposal: Reword SD-03.A; move the component and licence standard to SD-18.A.

defects.finding: Rejects and duplicates in a monitored queue is processing integrity error handling (PI1.2), not secure input validation.
defects.proposal: Move to SD-15.D.

defects.finding: Bundled approval of security requirements before build with the check before release that ISO27001:A.8.29 relies on.
defects.proposal: Reword SD-10.B; add SD-10.F for verification before release.

defects.finding: Each bundled two parts of ISO27001:A.8.15 with different evidence (source coverage with gap alerts; retention with protection from administrators). Retention was tested by interview alone.
defects.proposal: Reword B and C; add LM-02.F (gap alerts) and LM-02.G (protection); retention gains a settings test.

defects.finding: ISO27001:10.2 asks that corrective action is checked for effect; no objective tested it.
defects.proposal: Add LM-05.E.

defects.finding: ISO27001:A.5.28 is mapped on the evidence procedure but only the written plan was examined; LM-07.C bundled sharing the plan with reviewing it.
defects.proposal: Add LM-07.F (evidence handled as the plan sets) and LM-07.G (review); reword C to acknowledgement by role holders.

defects.finding: ISO27001:A.8.13 covers copies of software and systems; BC-01.A names them but nothing tested them. BC-01.D bundled storage protection with restore rights.
defects.proposal: Add BC-01.F (rebuild materials) and BC-01.E (restore rights); reword D with a settings test.

defects.finding: Bundled the redundancy each service relies on, and failover tests, with continuity planning (ISO27001:A.8.14 is its own Annex A control).
defects.proposal: Reword A and C; move redundancy and failover to BC-09.

defects.finding: Bundled the yearly register review with offboarding, an event per vendor with its own record; ISO27001:A.5.22 relies on removal with access revoked.
defects.proposal: Reword D; add BC-07.E (offboarding).

defects.finding: Bundled contract terms (ISO27001:A.5.20) with tracking of findings. ISO27001:A.5.22 and A.8.21 rationales rely on checking delivered service levels and no objective tested it.
defects.proposal: Reword E; add BC-08.F (findings) and BC-08.G (delivery review).

defects.finding: These rest on a person's judgement, a signature or a record no catalogued system holds: SD-01.E, SD-02.E, SD-04.C, SD-04.E, SD-07.D, SD-09.B, SD-09.C, SD-10.C, SD-10.D, SD-11.D, SD-12.E, SD-16.C, SD-18.C, LM-03.D, LM-04.D, LM-05.D, LM-05.E, LM-06.C, LM-06.D, LM-07.D, LM-07.E, LM-07.F, LM-10.B, LM-10.C, LM-12.B, LM-12.D, LM-12.E, BC-02.C, BC-03.B, BC-04.B, BC-06.C, BC-08.D, BC-10.C. People only artifacts: escrow-verification-record, notices-to-customers-of-subprocessor-changes, secure-coding-training-completion-for-developers.
defects.proposal: No fix; checks can show the record exists and is on time, not that it is right. The control page should say so.

defects.finding: No template exists; the vulnerability-management-policy-with-timeframes and dependency triage artifacts point at a policy that is not a template.
defects.proposal: Create a template, or use the operations-security-policy section 'Finding and fixing vulnerabilities'.

defects.finding: No template exists for a backup policy.
defects.proposal: Create a template, or use operations-security-policy 'Backups and restore tests' with the continuity plan Appendix B.

defects.finding: No template exists for the published subprocessor list.
defects.proposal: Create one, held as a Documents entry linked to BC-06.

defects.finding: No postmortem template ships, so verity.incidents.postmortem_recorded cannot read the content (timeline, impact, root cause, detection gap).
defects.proposal: Add a postmortem template.

defects.finding: Tasks has no incident marker and no notice decision field, yet the security incident register (LM-07.D) is meant to live there.
defects.proposal: Ship a Security incident task template with a structured notice decision field, or the Phase 3.1 Incidents module, before verity.incidents.registered can run. Imported incidents need source and external_id for the connector reconciliation checks.

defects.finding: Task templates are not bound to controls (template_id exists, the binding does not), so verity.tasks.change_approved_independently cannot find its population.
defects.proposal: Add a binding between task templates and controls.

defects.item: tasks: recurring series to control link
defects.finding: Recurring task series are not linked to controls.
defects.proposal: Link the series to the control through the links table for verity.tasks.recurring_review_on_time.

defects.finding: verity.tasks.remediation_in_sla covers tasks, not issue actions until they are promoted to tasks.
defects.proposal: verity.tasks.capa_on_time reads issue actions directly.

defects.finding: Vulnerability settings hold remediation days per severity but no triage time, so SD-03.D and verity.vulns.triaged_in_time have no parameter to test against.
defects.proposal: Add a triage time per severity to the vulnerability settings.

defects.finding: A maximum risk acceptance length is not a setting.
defects.proposal: Add a maximum acceptance length setting (default 12 months) for verity.vulns.acceptances_approved.

defects.finding: Imported vulnerability scan reports record findings, not the targets scanned, so scan coverage (LM-11.B, now LM-13.B) cannot be shown from Verity: a clean asset leaves no trace.
defects.proposal: Add a target list to vuln_reports.

defects.finding: Vendors have no flag for customer data as opposed to staff data; Verity does not publish the subprocessor list or record customer notices. vendor_subprocessors is fourth parties, not the company's list.
defects.proposal: Add a customer data flag on vendors and a published list document linked to BC-06.

defects.finding: vendor_discovered_apps has no connector source until an identity provider connector ships, so BC-05 is manual in P1. A reason for ignored apps needs confirming in the schema.
defects.proposal: Feed discovered apps from the Phase 2 identity provider connectors; confirm an ignore reason field.

defects.finding: The security terms required per tier are not a tiering policy setting, and code ownership and escrow are not contract fields (needed for BC-10).
defects.proposal: Add required terms per tier to the tiering policy, and code ownership and escrow fields to contracts.

defects.finding: ISO certificates are documents without structured period fields, so their validity cannot be evaluated like a SOC report review.
defects.proposal: Add structured validity dates for certificates.

defects.finding: capabilities.json lists GitHub under CI and CD as planned for Phase 2 although the GitHub connector exists. Deployments, workflow runs and check results need new read permissions (unverified), so ci.* checks are P2 even on GitHub.
defects.proposal: Make the capability listing say GitHub version control is live and GitHub CI and CD reads are Phase 2.

defects.finding: Says 81 tests, and Appendix C of control-framework-requirements.md says Verity tests are planned; checks.json has 93 checks and the 30 verity checks run.
defects.proposal: Regenerate the catalogue and update Appendix C.

defects.finding: The LM-01 text says devices have no source in the catalogue because device management is not planned, while capabilities.json lists device_management (jamf, kandji, intune). Extractor's note, the document does not raise the conflict.
defects.proposal: Reconcile with mdm-and-endpoint-strategy.md and the devices research.
